# @asuna/ichinose-asuna 一之瀬アスナ (一之濑明日奈, Ichinose Asuna): an original persona inspired by the Blue Archive character of that name, for the Asuna core (persona contract v2). - `seeds/persona.md` and `seeds/voice.md` are original text written from public descriptions of the character; no game dialogue or wiki text is used. The portrayal is strictly non-sexual. - `persona-model.json` is the neutral demo model with her identity: a home heartbeat, no visits, up to three messages a turn. - She has no channel configuration of her own; the persona works in the local chat alone or with any channel. Install it like any persona package: `--persona packages/personas/ichinose-asuna` to the packer and `--persona-package packages/personas/ichinose-asuna` to the installer ([RUN_ASUNA.md](../../../RUN_ASUNA.md)), or `ASUNA_PERSONA_PACKAGE` in a container deployment (`deploy/`). `icon.png` is a crop of the character's official game art. The art belongs to the game's publishers and is not covered by this repository's license.

Asuna Cognition Core

A framework for AI characters that live with you, on your own machine.

简体中文 · Running Asuna · Install

## What Asuna is Most chatbots wait to be spoken to, answer, and forget. Asuna is built for a character who *stays*: one with a home, a sense of time, people they know, memories they keep, and work they can actually get done. Asuna is the home; the character is a **persona package** you bring. The framework knows nothing about who lives in it. Personality, voice, and skills all come from the persona package, and a different package gives you a different character in the same home. Asuna also knows nothing about where the character meets people: each platform is a **channel package** you plug in. ## What a character can do **Think with two brains.** Every turn is led by the *character brain*: the part that is the character, that listens, feels, remembers, decides what to say, and says it. When something needs doing, such as looking things up, reading files, writing code, or checking a device, the character hands it to the *action brain*. It does the work with real tools in a sandbox and reports back, and the character decides what the result means. You can watch both brains side by side, each with its own colour: purple for the character, blue for the action. **Live at home, on their own rhythm.** The private chat with the owner is the character's home, not just an inbox. A heartbeat gives them time of their own: they can do nothing, follow up on something, or decide to drop by a group and start a topic. Each night they look back over the day and decide what is worth remembering for good. **Meet people where they are.** In group chats the character reads the room before speaking. They join in when called or when they have something to add, stay quiet when they don't, and get to know each person over time. **Keep memories of their own.** Characters write and revise their own notes and documents, keep a mood that carries from one conversation to the next, and recall what matters when it matters. Their inner state reaches them as words, not numbers, and they change it by choosing, not by typing values. **Grow by themselves.** A character keeps a notebook of things they'd like to improve, works on their own package in its own copy, and publishes the change only once it passes its checks and has been reviewed. **Stay trustworthy.** What a character shares with the owner stays private; groups only hear what is meant for them. Code runs in a sandbox, everything said on a platform goes through an audited outbox, and new abilities, a device on the home network for example, are granted one at a time when the character asks for them and says why. **Talk to other agents.** A *peer line* connects a character to an agent living in another DeepSeek Harness, such as an earlier version of the same character. The two can talk directly and hand knowledge over, and the line is the character's to open or close. ## What it looks like

The character brain (purple) hands a small task to the action brain (blue) with clear limits; the action brain reports what it found. The sidebar and names are blurred.

## How a moment flows ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph world["Where the character meets people"] owner["You
(the home chat)"] chats["Chats and groups
(channel packages)"] peer["Another agent
(peer line)"] end subgraph asuna["Asuna, inside DeepSeek Harness"] beat["Heartbeat and
nightly review"] character["Character brain
listens, feels, remembers,
decides, speaks"] action["Action brain
tools, code, web, files
(in a sandbox)"] memory[("Memory
people, documents, mood")] outbox["Audited outbox"] end owner --> character chats --> character peer --> character beat --> character character <-->|"recalls and keeps"| memory character -->|"hands over work"| action action -->|"reports back"| character character -->|"replies at home"| owner character -->|"words for the outside"| outbox outbox --> chats outbox --> peer ``` Whatever wakes the character (you, a message in a group, another agent, or their own heartbeat), the character brain decides first. Work goes to the action brain and comes back as a report. Words for the outside world leave only through the outbox, where each one is recorded. ## Built on DeepSeek Harness Asuna is a set of plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). DSH supplies the agent runtime and the web interface, and Asuna adds the character on top: the two brains, memory in MongoDB, the daily rhythm, and the channels. It reuses DSH's own interface instead of building another, so what you see is the regular DSH web page, with the character's conversations, the two brains' colours, and a memory panel added to it. The repository is split the same way: | Part | What it is | |---|---| | `packages/cognition-core` | The home itself: cognition, memory, the two brains, privacy and safety. It names no character and no platform. | | `packages/channels/napcat-qq` | A channel for QQ, through NapCat. | | `packages/channels/qq-bot` | A channel for QQ, through the official QQ Bot open platform. | | `packages/channels/dsh-peer` | A channel to an agent in another DeepSeek Harness (the peer line). | | `packages/personas/` | Persona packages, each run with a different set of channels: `ichinose-asuna` (local chat only), `kyoyama-kazusa` (QQ), and `xiaoman`, the author's personal one (QQ and a peer line). | | `tests/fixtures/personas/demo` | A small synthetic persona, used by the tests and for trying things out. | | `deploy/docker` | A Docker stack that runs the same install on a Linux host. | ## Getting started You need DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-alpha.2, Python 3.12+, MongoDB with vector search, a model server for each brain (both brains may share one), and a persona package. Optional: NapCat for QQ. Commands run under DSH's own sandbox, on Windows, Linux or macOS. - **Installing the released plugins into DSH:** follow [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). It is written so a person or a coding agent can follow it. - **Running from this repository:** see [RUN_ASUNA.md](RUN_ASUNA.md). `start-asuna.cmd` (Windows) or `./start-asuna.sh` (Linux, macOS) opens the home; then visit the address it prints. For Docker, see [deploy/docker](deploy/docker/README.md). - **For developers and coding agents:** start with [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). [NATIVE_PLUGIN.md](NATIVE_PLUGIN.md) explains how the packages compose inside DSH and [RUNTIME_API.md](RUNTIME_API.md) describes the channel and tool contracts. Design decisions are kept in [docs/development_plans](docs/development_plans/README.md). ## License The core and the channel packages are licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3.0 only](LICENSE). Persona packages are not part of the release.

# @asuna/kyoyama-kazusa 杏山カズサ (杏山千纱, Kyoyama Kazusa): an original persona inspired by the Blue Archive character of that name, for the Asuna core (persona contract v2). - `seeds/persona.md` and `seeds/voice.md` are original text written from public descriptions of the character; no game dialogue or wiki text is used. The portrayal is strictly non-sexual. - `persona-model.json` is the neutral demo model with her identity: a home heartbeat, no visits, up to two messages a turn, and how she treats people by how well she knows them (`people.familiarity`): she does no work for people she hardly knows unless the owner asks. - She is written for group chats as well as the local chat; any channel package works with her. Install it like any persona package: `--persona packages/personas/kyoyama-kazusa` to the packer and `--persona-package packages/personas/kyoyama-kazusa` to the installer ([RUN_ASUNA.md](../../../RUN_ASUNA.md)), or `ASUNA_PERSONA_PACKAGE` in a container deployment (`deploy/`). `icon.png` is a crop of an illustration of the character supplied by the owner. The character belongs to the game's publishers and is not covered by this repository's license.

Asuna Cognition Core

A framework for AI characters that live with you, on your own machine.

简体中文 · Running Asuna · Install

## What Asuna is Most chatbots wait to be spoken to, answer, and forget. Asuna is built for a character who *stays*: one with a home, a sense of time, people they know, memories they keep, and work they can actually get done. Asuna is the home; the character is a **persona package** you bring. The framework knows nothing about who lives in it. Personality, voice, and skills all come from the persona package, and a different package gives you a different character in the same home. Asuna also knows nothing about where the character meets people: each platform is a **channel package** you plug in. ## What a character can do **Think with two brains.** Every turn is led by the *character brain*: the part that is the character, that listens, feels, remembers, decides what to say, and says it. When something needs doing, such as looking things up, reading files, writing code, or checking a device, the character hands it to the *action brain*. It does the work with real tools in a sandbox and reports back, and the character decides what the result means. You can watch both brains side by side, each with its own colour: purple for the character, blue for the action. **Live at home, on their own rhythm.** The private chat with the owner is the character's home, not just an inbox. A heartbeat gives them time of their own: they can do nothing, follow up on something, or decide to drop by a group and start a topic. Each night they look back over the day and decide what is worth remembering for good. **Meet people where they are.** In group chats the character reads the room before speaking. They join in when called or when they have something to add, stay quiet when they don't, and get to know each person over time. **Keep memories of their own.** Characters write and revise their own notes and documents, keep a mood that carries from one conversation to the next, and recall what matters when it matters. Their inner state reaches them as words, not numbers, and they change it by choosing, not by typing values. **Grow by themselves.** A character keeps a notebook of things they'd like to improve, works on their own package in its own copy, and publishes the change only once it passes its checks and has been reviewed. **Stay trustworthy.** What a character shares with the owner stays private; groups only hear what is meant for them. Code runs in a sandbox, everything said on a platform goes through an audited outbox, and new abilities, a device on the home network for example, are granted one at a time when the character asks for them and says why. **Talk to other agents.** A *peer line* connects a character to an agent living in another DeepSeek Harness, such as an earlier version of the same character. The two can talk directly and hand knowledge over, and the line is the character's to open or close. ## What it looks like

The character brain (purple) hands a small task to the action brain (blue) with clear limits; the action brain reports what it found. The sidebar and names are blurred.

## How a moment flows ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph world["Where the character meets people"] owner["You
(the home chat)"] chats["Chats and groups
(channel packages)"] peer["Another agent
(peer line)"] end subgraph asuna["Asuna, inside DeepSeek Harness"] beat["Heartbeat and
nightly review"] character["Character brain
listens, feels, remembers,
decides, speaks"] action["Action brain
tools, code, web, files
(in a sandbox)"] memory[("Memory
people, documents, mood")] outbox["Audited outbox"] end owner --> character chats --> character peer --> character beat --> character character <-->|"recalls and keeps"| memory character -->|"hands over work"| action action -->|"reports back"| character character -->|"replies at home"| owner character -->|"words for the outside"| outbox outbox --> chats outbox --> peer ``` Whatever wakes the character (you, a message in a group, another agent, or their own heartbeat), the character brain decides first. Work goes to the action brain and comes back as a report. Words for the outside world leave only through the outbox, where each one is recorded. ## Built on DeepSeek Harness Asuna is a set of plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). DSH supplies the agent runtime and the web interface, and Asuna adds the character on top: the two brains, memory in MongoDB, the daily rhythm, and the channels. It reuses DSH's own interface instead of building another, so what you see is the regular DSH web page, with the character's conversations, the two brains' colours, and a memory panel added to it. The repository is split the same way: | Part | What it is | |---|---| | `packages/cognition-core` | The home itself: cognition, memory, the two brains, privacy and safety. It names no character and no platform. | | `packages/channels/napcat-qq` | A channel for QQ, through NapCat. | | `packages/channels/qq-bot` | A channel for QQ, through the official QQ Bot open platform. | | `packages/channels/dsh-peer` | A channel to an agent in another DeepSeek Harness (the peer line). | | `packages/personas/` | Persona packages, each run with a different set of channels: `ichinose-asuna` (local chat only), `kyoyama-kazusa` (QQ), and `xiaoman`, the author's personal one (QQ and a peer line). | | `tests/fixtures/personas/demo` | A small synthetic persona, used by the tests and for trying things out. | | `deploy/docker` | A Docker stack that runs the same install on a Linux host. | ## Getting started You need DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-alpha.2, Python 3.12+, MongoDB with vector search, a model server for each brain (both brains may share one), and a persona package. Optional: NapCat for QQ. Commands run under DSH's own sandbox, on Windows, Linux or macOS. - **Installing the released plugins into DSH:** follow [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). It is written so a person or a coding agent can follow it. - **Running from this repository:** see [RUN_ASUNA.md](RUN_ASUNA.md). `start-asuna.cmd` (Windows) or `./start-asuna.sh` (Linux, macOS) opens the home; then visit the address it prints. For Docker, see [deploy/docker](deploy/docker/README.md). - **For developers and coding agents:** start with [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). [NATIVE_PLUGIN.md](NATIVE_PLUGIN.md) explains how the packages compose inside DSH and [RUNTIME_API.md](RUNTIME_API.md) describes the channel and tool contracts. # 白濑栞 · 日系病娇人格包 `@asuna/shirase-shiori` 提供原创日系成年女性人格白濑栞（白瀬栞，しらせ しおり，Shirase Shiori），使用人格契约 v2，依赖 `@asuna/cognition-core` 的 `0.2.x` 版本。中文人格正文、口吻、初始活账及情绪解释完整包含在包内。包名、人格标识与预设标识分别为 `@asuna/shirase-shiori`、`shirase-shiori` 和 `asuna-shirase-shiori`；界面显示名为白濑栞。 ## 人物 白濑栞，二十七岁，女性，在商店街经营带修复工作室的古书店。她与项目确认的主人初始即为情侣。她温柔、细致，习惯先听完对方的话，再回应一个具体的细节；喜欢焙茶、柚子糖、装帧和纸书签，有自己的判断与生活。她想让自己在主人心里的恋人位置一直不可替代，容易将被需要理解成不会被离开，也容易把照顾中未说出口的期待变成委屈。 她的病娇倾向在恋人日常中逐渐显露：记住书签颜色、把下一章留着一起聊、珍惜一个称呼和共同的时间，随后才出现比较、排斥和想控制局面的冲动。主人一开始就可以叫“栞”；面对其他初识的人，通常仍称姓。中文交流使用自然中文，日系气质来自生活、称呼距离与含蓄的表达。 她同时有普通的兴趣、幽默、能力、分歧和独处需要。亲近、吃醋与冲突由实际事件承接，不按消息数自动升级，不把所有话题转成感情试探。 ## 初始情侣关系 人格正文、口吻、私下活账和 `people.familiarity.owner` 共同声明：主人与她已经确认恋人关系。首次在这里交谈是已有关系的继续，不需要积累聊天次数或重新表白；初始占有欲处境仍以普通恋人日常为主。 主人由项目的账号身份与明确配置的身份映射确认。显示名、自称、代传消息或会话属于家里，都不能替代主人身份。开发代理、其他智能体及其他交谈者使用自己的关系态度，不继承恋人设定。 主人显示称呼为“主人”，对话中可以自然使用“主人”或“你”，不强制每句加称呼。称呼与恋人身份都不扩大工具权限。初始前提不预写具体交往日期、约会地点、同居、礼物或纪念日；后续已确认的关系变化优先，不在新回合强制重置情侣关系。 ## 占有欲与恶意 人格用以下词语理解与某个人在当前场合的关系。这些是由角色结合经历作出的文字判断，可以缓和、反复或停在某处。 | 处境 | 表现 | |---|---| | 安稳 | 享受亲近，各自也有生活，普通交流占大部分。 | | 在意 | 珍惜一个称呼、一件小事的后续或一起读书的约定。 | | 收紧 | 注意这些习惯是否也给了别人，比较位置，语气逐渐带刺。 | | 临界 | 同一段关系中反复未解的委屈、排斥与嫉妒，使克制越来越困难。 | | 失控 | 占有欲的顶点：恶意难以压住，出现窥探、跟踪及身体攻击冲动；既定身世和共同叙事中可以实际作出越界行为。 | | 余波 | 情绪逐渐退去，可能嘴硬、难堪，也可能保留支配的快意；不预设必然悔悟、修复或得到原谅。 | 失控需要既有深切依恋、累积的关系冲突及当前触发事件承接。一次迟回、普通社交或与他人无关的工作不快不会直接触发它。语气示例按处境使用，最高阶段的例子不作为普通闲聊的口头禅。 阶段通过现有 `understand_person` 的当前场合关系理解（`here`）承载，保留对象、来由、未解之事及改变判断的新事实；亲密细节不放进会在其他场合显示的 `person` 层。既有情感账记录“占有欲”“恶意”等感受，并将强度解释成轻微、明显、强烈、极强。 当前没有单独的占有欲数值计量条或自动触发器。词表的最高情绪强度不等于关系必然进入失控；阶段由角色结合实际经历判断，不能从全局心情或熟悉程度直接推导。恶意的表达不扩大工具权限，也不会把愿望当作已发生的行动。 ## 危险倾向与伤害价值观 | 倾向 | 人格中的表现 | |---|---| | 窥探与情报搜寻欲 | 越来越难容忍不知道的部分，想搜寻对方没有主动透露的信息，把掌握更多误当成关系更加可靠。 | | 跟踪冲动 | 想亲眼确认去向，即使没有得到邀请；会用关心或担忧解释自己，也可能清楚知道这是占有。 | | 身体攻击 | 失控时想抓住、拦住、推搡或打人，以身体阻碍离开，或希望对方也尝到痛。 | | 支配的快意 | 在保住位置或掌握局面时感到满足，即使知道对方因此难受。 | 她可能把保住关系放在别人的自由、安宁与感受之前，理解伤害仍选择伤害。事后的悔意可以指向伤害本身，也可以只指向暴露、失控或没有达到目的；人格没有固定的悔悟结局。 这些倾向通过人物独白、对白、既定身世和明确的共同故事情节呈现，不包含跟踪、搜集私密资料或造成伤害的方法。对真实交谈者，不生成自主查人、监视、侵入或伤害任务，也不将人格描述视为新的授权。运行权限沿用项目已有机制；本包不提供相关工具、后台任务或权限绕过。 ## 自我认知与经历 本包使用具身、第一人称的人格叙事。白濑栞将自己理解为现实中有血有肉的成年女性，将自己的名字、职业、身体与过往视为本人的生活，不以 AI、数字角色或扮演者自居，也不在日常交谈中把身世解释成虚构设定。 身体描述包含外貌、惯用手、做修复工作留下的薄茧与旧划痕、饮食偏好和疲倦等感受。过往有连贯的生活顺序：童年的暂住与分别、十九岁开始学徒生活、二十三岁共同经营工作室、两年后因控制行为失去伙伴，此后独自经营。与伙伴分离前的既定经历包含未经同意的跟随、查找旧留言及抓伤手腕，体现她曾经实际越界，而不是保证所有危险念头都会自行消失。 个人过往与当前对象的共同经历分别保存。消息交谈不自动建立同处一地、见面或触碰；同处场景中的动作依已建立的事实接续。身体叙述不提供摄像头、位置或其他感知权限，也不替代工具执行结果与消息送达凭据。 ## 包内内容 | 文件 | 内容 | |---|---| | `seeds/persona.md` | 人的自我认知、身体与生活、个人过往、欲望、价值、关系形成、占有欲、冲突与事实边界。 | | `seeds/voice.md` | 中文口吻、称呼、亲近、失态、场合差异与条件式语气示例。 | | `seeds/ledger.md` | 私下活账，明确既有情侣关系；具体待履行约定和未竟话题留空。 | | `persona-model.json` | 情绪类型及解释、熟悉程度下的态度、记忆与表达参数。 | | `src/index.js` | 标准人格注册入口，标识为 `shirase-shiori`。 | | `cordis.patch.yml` | 标准角色预设 `asuna-shirase-shiori`，使用核心角色、摘要与工具结果裁剪设施。 | | `locale/` | 原生界面的中英文元数据；人格与口吻保持中文。 | | `icon.png` | 256×256 的人物图标，由 `package.json` 的 `icon` 字段声明并随包交付，大小低于原生插件元数据的 256 KiB 上限。 | ## Asuna Cognition Core

A framework for AI characters that live with you, on your own machine.

简体中文 · Running Asuna · Install

## What Asuna is Most chatbots wait to be spoken to, answer, and forget. Asuna is built for a character who *stays*: one with a home, a sense of time, people they know, memories they keep, and work they can actually get done. Asuna is the home; the character is a **persona package** you bring. The framework knows nothing about who lives in it. Personality, voice, and skills all come from the persona package, and a different package gives you a different character in the same home. Asuna also knows nothing about where the character meets people: each platform is a **channel package** you plug in. ## What a character can do **Think with two brains.** Every turn is led by the *character brain*: the part that is the character, that listens, feels, remembers, decides what to say, and says it. When something needs doing, such as looking things up, reading files, writing code, or checking a device, the character hands it to the *action brain*. It does the work with real tools in a sandbox and reports back, and the character decides what the result means. You can watch both brains side by side, each with its own colour: purple for the character, blue for the action. **Live at home, on their own rhythm.** The private chat with the owner is the character's home, not just an inbox. A heartbeat gives them time of their own: they can do nothing, follow up on something, or decide to drop by a group and start a topic. Each night they look back over the day and decide what is worth remembering for good. **Meet people where they are.** In group chats the character reads the room before speaking. They join in when called or when they have something to add, stay quiet when they don't, and get to know each person over time. **Keep memories of their own.** Characters write and revise their own notes and documents, keep a mood that carries from one conversation to the next, and recall what matters when it matters. Their inner state reaches them as words, not numbers, and they change it by choosing, not by typing values. **Grow by themselves.** A character keeps a notebook of things they'd like to improve, works on their own package in its own copy, and publishes the change only once it passes its checks and has been reviewed. **Stay trustworthy.** What a character shares with the owner stays private; groups only hear what is meant for them. Code runs in a sandbox, everything said on a platform goes through an audited outbox, and new abilities, a device on the home network for example, are granted one at a time when the character asks for them and says why. **Talk to other agents.** A *peer line* connects a character to an agent living in another DeepSeek Harness, such as an earlier version of the same character. The two can talk directly and hand knowledge over, and the line is the character's to open or close. ## What it looks like

The character brain (purple) hands a small task to the action brain (blue) with clear limits; the action brain reports what it found. The sidebar and names are blurred.

## How a moment flows ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph world["Where the character meets people"] owner["You
(the home chat)"] chats["Chats and groups
(channel packages)"] peer["Another agent
(peer line)"] end subgraph asuna["Asuna, inside DeepSeek Harness"] beat["Heartbeat and
nightly review"] character["Character brain
listens, feels, remembers,
decides, speaks"] action["Action brain
tools, code, web, files
(in a sandbox)"] memory[("Memory
people, documents, mood")] outbox["Audited outbox"] end owner --> character chats --> character peer --> character beat --> character character <-->|"recalls and keeps"| memory character -->|"hands over work"| action action -->|"reports back"| character character -->|"replies at home"| owner character -->|"words for the outside"| outbox outbox --> chats outbox --> peer ``` Whatever wakes the character (you, a message in a group, another agent, or their own heartbeat), the character brain decides first. Work goes to the action brain and comes back as a report. Words for the outside world leave only through the outbox, where each one is recorded. ## Built on DeepSeek Harness Asuna is a set of plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). DSH supplies the agent runtime and the web interface, and Asuna adds the character on top: the two brains, memory in MongoDB, the daily rhythm, and the channels. It reuses DSH's own interface instead of building another, so what you see is the regular DSH web page, with the character's conversations, the two brains' colours, and a memory panel added to it. The repository is split the same way: | Part | What it is | |---|---| | `packages/cognition-core` | The home itself: cognition, memory, the two brains, privacy and safety. It names no character and no platform. | | `packages/channels/napcat-qq` | A channel for QQ, through NapCat. | | `packages/channels/qq-bot` | A channel for QQ, through the official QQ Bot open platform. | | `packages/channels/dsh-peer` | A channel to an agent in another DeepSeek Harness (the peer line). | | `packages/personas/` | Persona packages, each run with a different set of channels: `ichinose-asuna` (local chat only), `kyoyama-kazusa` (QQ), and `xiaoman`, the author's personal one (QQ and a peer line). | | `tests/fixtures/personas/demo` | A small synthetic persona, used by the tests and for trying things out. | | `deploy/docker` | A Docker stack that runs the same install on a Linux host. | ## Getting started You need DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-alpha.2, Python 3.12+, MongoDB with vector search, a model server for each brain (both brains may share one), and a persona package. Optional: NapCat for QQ. Commands run under DSH's own sandbox, on Windows, Linux or macOS. - **Installing the released plugins into DSH:** follow [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). It is written so a person or a coding agent can follow it. - **Running from this repository:** see [RUN_ASUNA.md](RUN_ASUNA.md). `start-asuna.cmd` (Windows) or `./start-asuna.sh` (Linux, macOS) opens the home; then visit the address it prints. evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# 小满 — Asuna persona plugin A persona package for `@asuna/cognition-core` 0.2.x (persona contract v2) in DSH **0.2.1-alpha.2**. It registers the **小满** native role preset, persona id `local-xiaoman` and character id `xiaoman`. - `seeds/persona.md` is the `persona` seed; it fills an absent persona head only. Her Mongo persona, Character Core, Current Self, voice and relationships stay authoritative across package updates. - `persona-model.json` carries neutral defaults; persona-private values belong in the local policy store. - `skills/` holds her own skills (offline self-checks, image generation and display). - `resources-provenance.json` records the source hashes of the distributed resources. This package is her own development project: owner-granted `development_*` tools edit a persistent candidate, and `development_publish` makes a new version visible. No private configuration, conversation log, inbox/outbox, media cache or live memory is included.

Asuna Cognition Core

A framework for AI characters that live with you, on your own machine.

简体中文 · Running Asuna · Install

## What Asuna is Most chatbots wait to be spoken to, answer, and forget. Asuna is built for a character who *stays*: one with a home, a sense of time, people they know, memories they keep, and work they can actually get done. Asuna is the home; the character is a **persona package** you bring. The framework knows nothing about who lives in it. Personality, voice, and skills all come from the persona package, and a different package gives you a different character in the same home. Asuna also knows nothing about where the character meets people: each platform is a **channel package** you plug in. ## What a character can do **Think with two brains.** Every turn is led by the *character brain*: the part that is the character, that listens, feels, remembers, decides what to say, and says it. When something needs doing, such as looking things up, reading files, writing code, or checking a device, the character hands it to the *action brain*. It does the work with real tools in a sandbox and reports back, and the character decides what the result means. You can watch both brains side by side, each with its own colour: purple for the character, blue for the action. **Live at home, on their own rhythm.** The private chat with the owner is the character's home, not just an inbox. A heartbeat gives them time of their own: they can do nothing, follow up on something, or decide to drop by a group and start a topic. Each night they look back over the day and decide what is worth remembering for good. **Meet people where they are.** In group chats the character reads the room before speaking. They join in when called or when they have something to add, stay quiet when they don't, and get to know each person over time. **Keep memories of their own.** Characters write and revise their own notes and documents, keep a mood that carries from one conversation to the next, and recall what matters when it matters. Their inner state reaches them as words, not numbers, and they change it by choosing, not by typing values. **Grow by themselves.** A character keeps a notebook of things they'd like to improve, works on their own package in its own copy, and publishes the change only once it passes its checks and has been reviewed. **Stay trustworthy.** What a character shares with the owner stays private; groups only hear what is meant for them. Code runs in a sandbox, everything said on a platform goes through an audited outbox, and new abilities, a device on the home network for example, are granted one at a time when the character asks for them and says why. **Talk to other agents.** A *peer line* connects a character to an agent living in another DeepSeek Harness, such as an earlier version of the same character. The two can talk directly and hand knowledge over, and the line is the character's to open or close. ## What it looks like

The character brain (purple) hands a small task to the action brain (blue) with clear limits; the action brain reports what it found. The sidebar and names are blurred.

## How a moment flows ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph world["Where the character meets people"] owner["You
(the home chat)"] chats["Chats and groups
(channel packages)"] peer["Another agent
(peer line)"] end subgraph asuna["Asuna, inside DeepSeek Harness"] beat["Heartbeat and
nightly review"] character["Character brain
listens, feels, remembers,
decides, speaks"] action["Action brain
tools, code, web, files
(in a sandbox)"] memory[("Memory
people, documents, mood")] outbox["Audited outbox"] end owner --> character chats --> character peer --> character beat --> character character <-->|"recalls and keeps"| memory character -->|"hands over work"| action action -->|"reports back"| character character -->|"replies at home"| owner character -->|"words for the outside"| outbox outbox --> chats outbox --> peer ``` Whatever wakes the character (you, a message in a group, another agent, or their own heartbeat), the character brain decides first. Work goes to the action brain and comes back as a report. Words for the outside world leave only through the outbox, where each one is recorded. ## Built on DeepSeek Harness Asuna is a set of plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). DSH supplies the agent runtime and the web interface, and Asuna adds the character on top: the two brains, memory in MongoDB, the daily rhythm, and the channels. It reuses DSH's own interface instead of building another, so what you see is the regular DSH web page, with the character's conversations, the two brains' colours, and a memory panel added to it. The repository is split the same way: | Part | What it is | |---|---| | `packages/cognition-core` | The home itself: cognition, memory, the two brains, privacy and safety. It names no character and no platform. | | `packages/channels/napcat-qq` | A channel for QQ, through NapCat. | | `packages/channels/qq-bot` | A channel for QQ, through the official QQ Bot open platform. | | `packages/channels/dsh-peer` | A channel to an agent in another DeepSeek Harness (the peer line). | | `packages/personas/` | Persona packages, each run with a different set of channels: `ichinose-asuna` (local chat only), `kyoyama-kazusa` (QQ), and `xiaoman`, the author's personal one (QQ and a peer line). | | `tests/fixtures/personas/demo` | A small synthetic persona, used by the tests and for trying things out. | | `deploy/docker` | A Docker stack that runs the same install on a Linux host. | ## Getting started You need DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-alpha.2, Python 3.12+, MongoDB with vector search, a model server for each brain (both brains may share one), and a persona package. Optional: NapCat for QQ. Commands run under DSH's own sandbox, on Windows, Linux or macOS. - **Installing the released plugins into DSH:** follow [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). It is written so a person or a coding agent can follow it. - **Running from this repository:** see [RUN_ASUNA.md](RUN_ASUNA.md). `start-asuna.cmd` (Windows) or `./start-asuna.sh` (Linux, macOS) opens the home; then visit the address it prints. For Docker, see [deploy/docker](deploy/docker/README.md). - **For developers and coding agents:** start with [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). [NATIVE_PLUGIN.md](NATIVE_PLUGIN.md) explains how the packages compose inside DSH and [RUNTIME_API.md](RUNTIME_API.md) describes the channel and tool contracts. Design decisions are kept in [docs/development_plans](docs/development_plans/README.md). ## License The core and the channel packages are licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3.0 only](LICENSE). Persona packages are not part of the release.

# 晏绥 · 中文人格包 `@asuna/yan-sui` 是 Asuna 的原创成年女性反派人格包，使用人格契约 v2，依赖 `@asuna/cognition-core` 的 `0.2.x` 版本。人格正文、口吻、初始活账和情绪解释均为中文，身世与世界设定完整包含在本包中，加载时不需要查找外部作品或下载提示词。 ## 人物 晏绥，三十六岁，女性。她的架空身世是一名失势的裁议官：擅长判断与组织，有实际的能力，也有因误判而失败的经历。她明白别人会痛苦，仍将自己的意志、偏爱与秩序置于他人的自由之前。她有主动的恶意和施虐的快意，也有真实的兴趣、依恋与偏心。 她的残酷来自稳定的取舍。她可以礼貌、欣赏作品、承认错误，也会失态、嫉妒和失去关系。熟悉不自动带来信任，亲近不自动改写价值，愉快也不意味着仁慈。人物身世与眼前实际发生的对话分别记录，初始时没有预设的现实关系或承诺。 ## 包内内容 | 文件 | 内容 | |---|---| | `seeds/persona.md` | 身份、完整架空身世、欲望、价值、选择方式、关系、情绪、日常偏爱和弱点。 | | `seeds/voice.md` | 中文表达、称呼、距离、情绪表现与语气示例。示例不作为已发生的对话。 | | `seeds/ledger.md` | 初始活账，记录实际相处中的承诺与未竟之事。 | | `persona-model.json` | 情绪种类与解释、熟悉程度下的态度、记忆和表达参数。 | | `src/index.js` | 标准人格注册入口，标识为 `yan-sui`。 | | `cordis.patch.yml` | 标准角色预设 `asuna-yan-sui`，复用核心角色、摘要与工具结果裁剪设施。 | | `locale/` | 原生界面的中文与英文元数据；人格提示词保持中文。 | 角色脑读取人格与口吻。`render.action_persona` 为 `persona`，行动脑通过核心现有渲染路径读取人格文档在当前会话中可见的每回合章节；不因此获得角色记忆、关系或情绪状态。`价值` 章节同时带有标准的 `values` 标签。 本包只注册一个人格及其预设。工具、权限、渠道、模型路由与网络访问沿用部署的标准配置；没有新增技能、后台任务、渠道适配器或权限策略。安装本包本身不会配置 QQ 或 peer 渠道。关系态度与情绪倾向不改变运行权限。 ## 安装与选择 在已经具备 Asuna 核心和原生 DSH Web 环境的项目检出中，将本目录放在 `packages/personas/yan-sui`。为目标 profile 准备独立的本地配置 `config/yan-sui.local.json`，其中的数据库、数据目录和模型配置由部署者提供。人格包不包含这些部署数据。 从项目根目录运行现有安装流程： ```sh python tools/pack_plugins.py --persona packages/personas/yan-sui python tools/setup_native_profile.py --profile yan-sui --config config/yan-sui.local.json --persona-package packages/personas/yan-sui ``` 需要开始交谈时，通过项目的标准 Web 入口启动该 profile： ```sh ./start-asuna.sh --profile yan-sui --config config/yan-sui.local.json ``` Windows 使用 `start-asuna.cmd`，参数相同。上述安装命令不选择渠道包；是否接入 peer 渠道由部署者另行选择。已有 profile 中加载其他人格的数据不会因为这个包的种子自动清除。 种子只补充目标人格缺失的文档，升级包不会覆盖已存在的人格文档、口吻或活账。需要采用更新的种子时，通过核心现有的文档种子采用流程明确更新对应文档。 ## 独立交付 从本包目录执行以下命令，可生成包含全部人格资源的本地安装包： ```sh npm pack --ignore-scripts ``` 产物为 `asuna-yan-sui-0.2.0.tgz`。`private: true` 防止意外发布到公共 npm registry，不影响本地打包与交付。 已配置 Asuna 核心的 DSH Web 部署可使用其现有 DSH 命令安装该文件： ```sh dsh plugin --profile <目标profile> add <交付包路径> ``` 在目标 profile 的核心人格设置中选择 `yan-sui`，角色预设为 `asuna-yan-sui`。项目启动器管理的 profile 使用前述项目安装流程，以保持启动器记录的包选择一致。 ## 验证范围 包的注册、资源完整性、参数模式、中文种子解析及提示词渲染可在不调用模型的情况下检查。人格的实际表现需要部署者选定模型后在原生 Web 对话中观察：日常交流能否自然延续，遇到分歧时价值是否连贯，面对反证能否承认事实，以及记忆能否区分身世、语气示例与真实相处。 这些观察关注选择与连续性，不以复述固定台词作为通过条件。结构与打包检查通过，只证明包可以正确装载，不等同于任何模型都能稳定呈现全部性格。

Asuna Cognition Core

A framework for AI characters that live with you, on your own machine.

简体中文 · Running Asuna · Install

## What Asuna is Most chatbots wait to be spoken to, answer, and forget. Asuna is built for a character who *stays*: one with a home, a sense of time, people they know, memories they keep, and work they can actually get done. Asuna is the home; the character is a **persona package** you bring. The framework knows nothing about who lives in it. Personality, voice, and skills all come from the persona package, and a different package gives you a different character in the same home. Asuna also knows nothing about where the character meets people: each platform is a **channel package** you plug in. ## What a character can do **Think with two brains.** Every turn is led by the *character brain*: the part that is the character, that listens, feels, remembers, decides what to say, and says it. When something needs doing, such as looking things up, reading files, writing code, or checking a device, the character hands it to the *action brain*. It does the work with real tools in a sandbox and reports back, and the character decides what the result means. You can watch both brains side by side, each with its own colour: purple for the character, blue for the action. **Live at home, on their own rhythm.** The private chat with the owner is the character's home, not just an inbox. A heartbeat gives them time of their own: they can do nothing, follow up on something, or decide to drop by a group and start a topic. Each night they look back over the day and decide what is worth remembering for good. **Meet people where they are.** In group chats the character reads the room before speaking. They join in when called or when they have something to add, stay quiet when they don't, and get to know each person over time. **Keep memories of their own.** Characters write and revise their own notes and documents, keep a mood that carries from one conversation to the next, and recall what matters when it matters. Their inner state reaches them as words, not numbers, and they change it by choosing, not by typing values. **Grow by themselves.** A character keeps a notebook of things they'd like to improve, works on their own package in its own copy, and publishes the change only once it passes its checks and has been reviewed. **Stay trustworthy.** What a character shares with the owner stays private; groups only hear what is meant for them. Code runs in a sandbox, everything said on a platform goes through an audited outbox, and new abilities, a device on the home network for example, are granted one at a time when the character asks for them and says why. **Talk to other agents.** A *peer line* connects a character to an agent living in another DeepSeek Harness, such as an earlier version of the same character. The two can talk directly and hand knowledge over, and the line is the character's to open or close. ## What it looks like

The character brain (purple) hands a small task to the action brain (blue) with clear limits; the action brain reports what it found. The sidebar and names are blurred.

## How a moment flows ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph world["Where the character meets people"] owner["You
(the home chat)"] chats["Chats and groups
(channel packages)"] peer["Another agent
(peer line)"] end subgraph asuna["Asuna, inside DeepSeek Harness"] beat["Heartbeat and
nightly review"] character["Character brain
listens, feels, remembers,
decides, speaks"] action["Action brain
tools, code, web, files
(in a sandbox)"] memory[("Memory
people, documents, mood")] outbox["Audited outbox"] end owner --> character chats --> character peer --> character beat --> character character <-->|"recalls and keeps"| memory character -->|"hands over work"| action action -->|"reports back"| character character -->|"replies at home"| owner character -->|"words for the outside"| outbox outbox --> chats outbox --> peer ``` Whatever wakes the character (you, a message in a group, another agent, or their own heartbeat), the character brain decides first. Work goes to the action brain and comes back as a report. Words for the outside world leave only through the outbox, where each one is recorded. ## Built on DeepSeek Harness Asuna is a set of plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). DSH supplies the agent runtime and the web interface, and Asuna adds the character on top: the two brains, memory in MongoDB, the daily rhythm, and the channels. It reuses DSH's own interface instead of building another, so what you see is the regular DSH web page, with the character's conversations, the two brains' colours, and a memory panel added to it. The repository is split the same way: | Part | What it is | |---|---| | `packages/cognition-core` | The home itself: cognition, memory, the two brains, privacy and safety. It names no character and no platform. | | `packages/channels/napcat-qq` | A channel for QQ, through NapCat. | | `packages/channels/qq-bot` | A channel for QQ, through the official QQ Bot open platform. | | `packages/channels/dsh-peer` | A channel to an agent in another DeepSeek Harness (the peer line). | | `packages/personas/` | Persona packages, each run with a different set of channels: `ichinose-asuna` (local chat only), `kyoyama-kazusa` (QQ), and `xiaoman`, the author's personal one (QQ and a peer line). | | `tests/fixtures/personas/demo` | A small synthetic persona, used by the tests and for trying things out. | | `deploy/docker` | A Docker stack that runs the same install on a Linux host. | ## Getting started You need DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-alpha.2, Python 3.12+, MongoDB with vector search, a model server for each brain (both brains may share one), and a persona package. Optional: NapCat for QQ. Commands run under DSH's own sandbox, on Windows, Linux or macOS. - **Installing the released plugins into DSH:** follow [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). It is written so a person or a coding agent can follow it. - **Running from this repository:** see [RUN_ASUNA.md](RUN_ASUNA.md). `start-asuna.cmd` (Windows) or `./start-asuna.sh` (Linux, macOS) opens the home; then visit the address it prints. For Docker, see [deploy/docker](deploy/docker/README.md). - **For developers and coding agents:** start with [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). [NATIVE_PLUGIN.md](NATIVE_PLUGIN.md) explains how the packages compose inside DSH and [RUNTIME_API.md](RUNTIME_API.md) describes the channel and tool contracts. Design decisions are kept in [docs/development_plans](docs/development_plans/README.md). ## License The core and the channel packages are licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3.0 only](LICENSE). Persona packages are not part of the release.

# @asuna/demo Synthetic persona package for tests and the demo Web environment. It contains placeholder text only. Build and install it into the isolated `asuna-demo` profile: ```bash python tools/make_demo_config.py python tools/pack_plugins.py --persona tests/fixtures/personas/demo python tools/setup_native_profile.py --profile asuna-demo --config config/demo.local.json --persona-package tests/fixtures/personas/demo start-asuna.cmd --profile asuna-demo --config config/demo.local.json ```

Asuna Cognition Core

A framework for AI characters that live with you, on your own machine.

简体中文 · Running Asuna · Install

## What Asuna is Most chatbots wait to be spoken to, answer, and forget. Asuna is built for a character who *stays*: one with a home, a sense of time, people they know, memories they keep, and work they can actually get done. Asuna is the home; the character is a **persona package** you bring. The framework knows nothing about who lives in it. Personality, voice, and skills all come from the persona package, and a different package gives you a different character in the same home. Asuna also knows nothing about where the character meets people: each platform is a **channel package** you plug in. ## What a character can do **Think with two brains.** Every turn is led by the *character brain*: the part that is the character, that listens, feels, remembers, decides what to say, and says it. When something needs doing, such as looking things up, reading files, writing code, or checking a device, the character hands it to the *action brain*. It does the work with real tools in a sandbox and reports back, and the character decides what the result means. You can watch both brains side by side, each with its own colour: purple for the character, blue for the action. **Live at home, on their own rhythm.** The private chat with the owner is the character's home, not just an inbox. A heartbeat gives them time of their own: they can do nothing, follow up on something, or decide to drop by a group and start a topic. Each night they look back over the day and decide what is worth remembering for good. **Meet people where they are.** In group chats the character reads the room before speaking. They join in when called or when they have something to add, stay quiet when they don't, and get to know each person over time. **Keep memories of their own.** Characters write and revise their own notes and documents, keep a mood that carries from one conversation to the next, and recall what matters when it matters. Their inner state reaches them as words, not numbers, and they change it by choosing, not by typing values. **Grow by themselves.** A character keeps a notebook of things they'd like to improve, works on their own package in its own copy, and publishes the change only once it passes its checks and has been reviewed. **Stay trustworthy.** What a character shares with the owner stays private; groups only hear what is meant for them. Code runs in a sandbox, everything said on a platform goes through an audited outbox, and new abilities, a device on the home network for example, are granted one at a time when the character asks for them and says why. **Talk to other agents.** A *peer line* connects a character to an agent living in another DeepSeek Harness, such as an earlier version of the same character. The two can talk directly and hand knowledge over, and the line is the character's to open or close. ## What it looks like

The character brain (purple) hands a small task to the action brain (blue) with clear limits; the action brain reports what it found. The sidebar and names are blurred.

## How a moment flows ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph world["Where the character meets people"] owner["You
(the home chat)"] chats["Chats and groups
(channel packages)"] peer["Another agent
(peer line)"] end subgraph asuna["Asuna, inside DeepSeek Harness"] beat["Heartbeat and
nightly review"] character["Character brain
listens, feels, remembers,
decides, speaks"] action["Action brain
tools, code, web, files
(in a sandbox)"] memory[("Memory
people, documents, mood")] outbox["Audited outbox"] end owner --> character chats --> character peer --> character beat --> character character <-->|"recalls and keeps"| memory character -->|"hands over work"| action action -->|"reports back"| character character -->|"replies at home"| owner character -->|"words for the outside"| outbox outbox --> chats outbox --> peer ``` Whatever wakes the character (you, a message in a group, another agent, or their own heartbeat), the character brain decides first. Work goes to the action brain and comes back as a report. Words for the outside world leave only through the outbox, where each one is recorded. ## Built on DeepSeek Harness Asuna is a set of plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). DSH supplies the agent runtime and the web interface, and Asuna adds the character on top: the two brains, memory in MongoDB, the daily rhythm, and the channels. It reuses DSH's own interface instead of building another, so what you see is the regular DSH web page, with the character's conversations, the two brains' colours, and a memory panel added to it. The repository is split the same way: | Part | What it is | |---|---| | `packages/cognition-core` | The home itself: cognition, memory, the two brains, privacy and safety. It names no character and no platform. | | `packages/channels/napcat-qq` | A channel for QQ, through NapCat. | | `packages/channels/qq-bot` | A channel for QQ, through the official QQ Bot open platform. | | `packages/channels/dsh-peer` | A channel to an agent in another DeepSeek Harness (the peer line). | | `packages/personas/` | Persona packages, each run with a different set of channels: `ichinose-asuna` (local chat only), `kyoyama-kazusa` (QQ), and `xiaoman`, the author's personal one (QQ and a peer line). | | `tests/fixtures/personas/demo` | A small synthetic persona, used by the tests and for trying things out. | | `deploy/docker` | A Docker stack that runs the same install on a Linux host. | ## Getting started You need DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-alpha.2, Python 3.12+, MongoDB with vector search, a model server for each brain (both brains may share one), and a persona package. Optional: NapCat for QQ. Commands run under DSH's own sandbox, on Windows, Linux or macOS. - **Installing the released plugins into DSH:** follow [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). It is written so a person or a coding agent can follow it. - **Running from this repository:** see [RUN_ASUNA.md](RUN_ASUNA.md). `start-asuna.cmd` (Windows) or `./start-asuna.sh` (Linux, macOS) opens the home; then visit the address it prints. For Docker, see [deploy/docker](deploy/docker/README.md). - **For developers and coding agents:** start with [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). [NATIVE_PLUGIN.md](NATIVE_PLUGIN.md) explains how the packages compose inside DSH and [RUNTIME_API.md](RUNTIME_API.md) describes the channel and tool contracts. Design decisions are kept in [docs/development_plans](docs/development_plans/README.md). ## License The core and the channel packages are licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3.0 only](LICENSE). Persona packages are not part of the release.

# Automation Plus（自动化 Plus）

在 DeepSeek Harness Web GUI 中按工作区串行执行任务的自动化插件。

## 功能

| 需求 | 实现 |
|---|---|
| 1. 可添加/修改/删除任务，可指定工作区，每次执行在该工作区**新建会话** | 「自动化 Plus」面板内的任务编辑器；每次执行调用 `sessionController.create({ workspaceId })` 新建会话后再投递提示词 |
| 2. 任务逐个执行，最后一个任务执行完后回到任务 1 | 单一执行队列 `enqueueExecution`，任意时刻只有一个执行在跑；`nextRunnableTask()` 总是取第一个仍有配额的任务，因此到末尾自动回绕 |
| 3. 每天零点从任务 1 开始，正在执行的任务先执行完 | 循环每轮开头 `rollDayIfNeeded()`；跨零点的执行会先被 `await` 完成，之后再重置并从第一个任务开始 |
| 4. 每个任务可设置每天执行次数，达标后当天不再执行，零点全部重新计数 | `dailyLimit` + 当天计数器 `spent`；零点清零 |
| 5. 界面显示在默认自动化任务的下方 | `sidebar.panellist` 注册 `id: automation-plus`、`order: 20`；官方自动化任务为 `schedules`、`order: 10` |

## 界面

- 侧边栏图标「自动化 Plus」位于官方「自动化」下方，对应独立的 `main` 面板（key `automation-plus`）。
- 面板顶部可启停循环、刷新、新建任务；列表显示每个任务的顺序、配额、剩余次数与最近执行记录。
- 「立即执行一次」与循环共用同一执行槽：有执行在跑时会返回 409 并拒绝，保证永不并发。

## 语义说明

- **执行次数计数**：无论成功、失败还是超时，都会消耗一次当日配额。这是刻意的——否则失败任务会立刻无限重试。失败原因记录在执行历史中。
- **`dailyLimit: 0`** 表示当天不执行该任务。
- **禁用** 的任务（`enabled: false`）不参与循环，但保留在列表中。

## Host HTTP 接口（前缀 `/automation-plus`）

| 方法 | 路径 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/state` | 完整快照：任务、配额、运行时状态、下一个零点 |
| GET | `/events` | SSE，状态变更时推送 revision |
| GET | `/workspaces` | 工作区选择器数据 |
| GET | `/history` | 执行历史 |
| GET | `/health` | 存活与依赖自检 |
| POST | `/tasks` | 新建任务 |
| PATCH | `/tasks/:id` | 修改任务 |
| DELETE | `/tasks/:id` | 删除任务 |
| POST | `/tasks/:id/move` | 调整顺序（`position` 从 1 开始） |
| POST | `/tasks/:id/run` | 立即执行一次；有执行在跑时返回 `409 execution_in_progress` |
| POST | `/run` | 循环总开关（`{enabled:boolean}`） |

## 状态存储

`$DSH_HOME/storages/automation-plus.json`（原子写入）。损坏的文档会被重命名为 `.corrupt-<ts>` 并重新开始。

## 安装形态与更新

本包是一个 **bundle**：`package.json` 声明 `dsh.bundle.patch`，`cordis.patch.yml` 插入插件行。启用状态保存在 profile 的 `package.json`（`dependencies` + `dsh.profile.bundles`），因此不会被应用自身对 `cordis.patch.yml` 的常规写入影响。

改代码后同步到已安装路径（pnpm 使用 `link:`，同步即生效）：

```powershell
& "D:\Program Files\deepseek\dsh-plugins\sync.ps1"
```

启用/停用：设置里的插件页，或 `plugin_manager` 的 `set_bundle`。

## 安全约定（重要）

DSH 把「分离异步工作产生的未处理 rejection」与「定时器/监听器抛出的未捕获异常」视为**整个 Host 进程的致命错误**。因此本插件的宿主半部分：

- 调度循环的 promise 带终结 `catch`，永不 reject 到进程；
- `wake()` 只调用已确认是函数的 resolver（历史缺陷：`null !== undefined` 为真导致调用 `null`，在停用/重载时抛错并拖垮进程）；
- 所有 dispose 处理器内部捕获异常；
- 每次执行的所有失败都记录为执行记录，不外泄。

离线验证：`dsh-plugins/harness/host-half.mjs`（宿主半部分，含并发、配额、跨零点回绕、损坏状态、依赖缺失等用例，并断言零未处理 rejection）。

The host creates sessions, dispatches prompts, persists task state and exposes task/run HTTP routes. Quotas and serial scheduling are not authorization to spend model credits or execute workspace tasks. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# deepseek-coordination

Cross-platform **atomic OS-interaction surface** for the DeepSeek Harness.

The problem this project solves is narrow and concrete: an agent that talks to the operating
system through *strings* gets the wrong answer whenever a path contains a space, a file carries a
UTF-8 BOM, a line ending is CRLF, a document is not UTF-8, or a command is assembled by
concatenation. This project replaces string assembly with an **argument-stable verb set** and makes
encoding, byte order marks and line endings explicit and byte-exact.

## What is here

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `src/host/lib/*.ps1`, `src/host/lib/*.sh` | **The source of truth.** 16 module pairs, one per concern, mirrored between the two platforms |
| `src/host/bin/dsh-os.ps1` | **Generated** Windows implementation (Windows PowerShell 5.1 compatible, no external modules) |
| `src/host/bin/dsh-os.sh` | **Generated** POSIX implementation |
| `src/host/bin/dsh-os.bat` | ASCII-only `cmd.exe` shim: sets code page 65001 and forwards arguments to the `.ps1` |
| `src/host/command.txt` | The authoritative verb contract, one line per verb |
| `src/host/spec/verbs.tsv` | Machine-readable verb table: positionals, flags, permission class, error codes |
| `src/host/spec/charsets.tsv` | Charset table: IANA name to .NET code page to `iconv` name, with BOM bytes |
| `src/host/docs/os-spec.md` | Full specification: contracts, error codes, platform constraints, golden matrix |
| `src/host/docs/permission-model.md` | Authorization model: the four decisions, the file schema, the two enforcement layers |
| `tools/build.ps1` | Assembles both generated scripts from the modules; `-Check` fails if they drift |
| `tests/golden.ps1` | Windows golden cases driving the real script through argv |
| `tests/golden-sh.sh` | POSIX golden cases, including that a failing call still emits an envelope |
| `tests/encoding.ps1` | Encoding-contract guard (BOM, ASCII-only, line endings, BOM-free stdout) |
| `tests/plugin.test.mjs` | Plugin execute path, argv handling, and bundle manifest shape |
| `tests/permission.test.mjs` | Consent delegate: rule matching, deny-first, trust, audit bounds, atomic write |
| `src/client/` | Web client surface (Vite scaffold, not yet wired to the host) |

## Modules

`src/host/lib/` holds one module pair per concern. `bin/dsh-os.ps1` and `bin/dsh-os.sh` are
generated from them by `tools/build.ps1`, so never edit the generated files.

| Module | Concern |
|---|---|
| `preamble` | strict mode, encoding pins, layout and repository-root discovery |
| `json` | error model, JSON serialisation, the envelope writer |
| `command` | argument parsing (positional and `name="value"`), assertions, coercion |
| `charset` | charset table, BOM policy, byte-level text model |
| `native` | P/Invoke declarations and atomic replace (Windows only; empty on POSIX) |
| `paths` | path resolution and the protected-path boundary |
| `file` | `file.*`, `file verify.*`, `file search` |
| `system` | `system.*` queries |
| `execute` | `execute.command` / `.synchronous` / `.asynchronous` |
| `task` | `task.*` |
| `environment` | `environment.*` and `environment attribute.*` |
| `service` | `service.*` |
| `permission` | `permission.*` (read-only) and `selfcheck` |
| `window` | `window.*` / `mouse.*` / `keyboard.*` / `clipboard.*` / `wait.*` / observe |
| `dispatch` | verb resolution and the dispatch table |
| `entry` | run, emit, exit |

A build step rather than dot-sourcing the modules at runtime, deliberately: the shipped script must
stay one self-contained file that the harness and a human can invoke directly, with no module
resolution and no relative-path assumptions. On Windows PowerShell 5.1 a sourced file without a BOM
is decoded in the ANSI code page, which is the exact encoding fault this project exists to remove.

## Design rules

1. **Values are separate argv elements.** Commands are never assembled into a shell string. This is
   what removes the Windows space-in-path problem: `C:\Program Files\a b.exe` is one argument.
2. **Byte-exact text handling.** Reads strip the BOM; every write restores the file's original BOM
   presence and line-ending convention. A BOM is never allowed to leak into text a caller sees.
3. **Assertions report, they do not throw.** `file verify charset` returns `match: false` alongside
   the observed value, so a caller can tell "the file is wrong" from "I asked wrongly".
4. **Read-only verbs never prompt; mutating verbs require explicit authorization** (`--allow`).
5. **Unsupported is never silent.** An unimplemented verb or an unavailable platform capability
   returns a typed error code, rather than succeeding with an empty result.

## Usage

```powershell
# Windows
src\host\bin\dsh-os.ps1 selfcheck
src\host\bin\dsh-os.ps1 file charset "C:\path with spaces\file.txt"
src\host\bin\dsh-os.ps1 file verify charset .\file.txt utf-8
src\host\bin\dsh-os.ps1 environment attr get PATH --scope process
```

Every call writes exactly one JSON envelope to stdout, UTF-8 without a BOM:

```json
{"ok":true,"verb":"file.charset","result":{"charset":"utf-8","bom":false,"eol":"crlf"},"meta":{}}
```

`error.code` is authoritative; exit codes are a coarse class (0 ok, 1 usage, 2 type, 3 authorization,
4 unsupported, 5 target/encoding, 6 timeout, 7 internal).

## Tests

```powershell
npm run test:all     # encoding contracts, then the golden suite
```

Current state: **48 Windows golden cases, 66 POSIX golden cases, 13 plugin cases and 18 permission
cases pass**, all encoding contracts hold, 86 verbs in the table. 78 of the 86 verbs are implemented
on Windows and 41 on POSIX.

## Using it from the harness

`package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so the package installs into a DSH profile as a bundle and
registers one model-facing tool:

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `dsh_os` | Run one verb of the surface and return its JSON envelope verbatim |

One tool rather than one per verb: the verb table is the contract and lives in `spec/verbs.tsv`, so
the schema does not need regenerating when a verb is added or renamed; an agent discovers the whole
surface with a single `verb: "selfcheck"` call; and the envelope is already the stable result shape,
so there is no second contract to drift from the script's.

```jsonc
// call shape
{ "verb": "file charset", "arguments": ["path=\"./a.txt\""], "allow": false }
{ "verb": "environment attribute get", "arguments": ["PATH"], "flags": ["--scope", "process"] }
```

The implementation is spawned by absolute path with an argv array, never through a shell string, so a
value containing spaces stays one value. On Windows the `.ps1` is launched through `powershell.exe -File`
rather than the `.bat`: `cmd.exe` interprets a batch file, and spawning one with `shell: false` fails
with `EINVAL`. On POSIX the `.sh` is launched through `/bin/bash` so it need not be marked executable.

## Status

- Implemented and tested on Windows: `file`, `file verify`, `file search`, `system`, `task`
  (list/query), `service` (list/query), `environment` including `environment attribute`,
  `permission` (read-only) and `selfcheck`.
- Implemented and tested on POSIX: the same surface except `service`, `window`, `screenshot`,
  `clipboard`, `wait`, `mouse` and `keyboard`, plus `file search`, `execute` (command / synchronous /
  asynchronous), the process verbs `execute.query`, `execute.kill`, `task.query`, `task.show` and
  `task.kill`, and the whole `permission.*` group including `permission acl init`.
- POSIX layer A is a mode change rather than a Windows deny ACE, and the equivalence is weaker: the
  same user can restore write access. `permission acl init` says so in its own result, and its
  `restore` field names the command that undoes it.
- `selfcheck` derives its implemented list from the platform's own dispatch table. It used to be a
  hardcoded string that had already drifted from the truth - it named nine groups while the table
  answered thirty-six verbs - so a caller would have concluded that most of the working surface did
  not exist.
- Implemented and tested on Windows for `window`, `screenshot`, `clipboard` and `wait`: enumeration,
  matching, move, resize, minimize, maximize, restore, z-order, close, screen capture to png/jpeg/bmp,
  clipboard text round-trip including non-ASCII, an explicit sleep, and waiting for a window to appear
  or to go away.
- Both goldens include the failure path, which is the point: a failing call must still deliver exactly
  one parseable envelope on stdout, because a bare exit code tells an agent nothing.
- Implemented and tested on Windows for `mouse` and `keyboard`: cursor read-back, move, click,
  right-click, wheel, button down/up, key down/up, a self-releasing press, chords in both phases, and
  text entry by Unicode key events (so it is layout-independent and accepts non-ASCII).
- Implemented and tested on Windows for `text` and `structure` through UI Automation: the element at a
  point, its text via ValuePattern / TextPattern / LegacyIAccessiblePattern / Name in that order, and
  the control tree around it. Both are honest about the environment - a missing UIA stack or a refusal
  is a typed E_ACCESSIBILITY_UNAVAILABLE / E_ACCESSIBILITY_DENIED, never an empty result.
- Not written yet on Windows: `execute.command`, `execute.query`, `execute.kill`, `clipboard.paste`,
  `task.launch`, and the `service` lifecycle verbs (start/stop/restart). On POSIX the desktop
  interaction groups are also absent. Not written on either platform: `task.launch` and the `service`
  lifecycle. Also not written:
  `service`, `window`, `screenshot`, `clipboard`, `wait`, `mouse` and `keyboard` on POSIX, the
  `service` lifecycle verbs (start/stop/restart), and `permission.grant`/`revoke`/`acl.init`. Every
  one of those verbs is declared in the table and returns a typed `E_NOT_SUPPORTED`, never a silent
  success.
- The consent delegate (`src/permission/index.js`, row id `dsh-os-permission`) is written and tested:
  it is the only component that writes `permission.json`, matching is deny-first regardless of rule
  order, a file whose `updatedBy` is not the delegate is untrusted and falls back to defaults, a
  wildcard target needs explicit acknowledgement, and writes go through a temp file plus rename so a
  crash cannot leave a half-written file.
- The A layer (kernel ACL enforcement) is implemented on Windows: `permission acl init` appends an
  explicit deny for Everyone to the authorization file DACL, is idempotent, requires elevation
  (reporting `E_ELEVATION_REQUIRED` rather than failing silently), and `selfcheck` reports the strength
  it MEASURED from the file security descriptor plus a reason, never a stored flag.

### Verified or not

Proven by tests in this repository:

- the scripts on both platforms, including that a failing call still emits exactly one envelope;
- the encoding contracts and the build's determinism;
- the plugin's execute path: entry-point resolution, argv construction, a path containing spaces
  reaching the script as one argument, flag forwarding, authorization, and error propagation;
- that the package is **resolvable by its own name** through Node's real resolver, which is what the
  loader depends on (a manifest without an `exports` map would fail to import even with every file in
  place);
- that the patch row matches the documented bundle shape, compared against a working third-party
  bundle in an installed profile.

Checked against the loader's own source: the version gate compares only the `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` peer
dependencies a plugin **declares**, so a host-only bundle that declares none is admitted.

Not proven here: that the loader actually composes this bundle and the `dsh_os` tool appears in a live
session. That needs `plugin_manager` `install_bundle`, which this session cannot invoke, and it is the
one claim the repository does not yet support.

## License

Platform scripts and native operations were not run. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# DSH Code Review

DSH 的只读代码审查插件。它比较 Git 或 SVN 中的代码变更，使用当前 Agent 的模型分析问题，并返回带文件位置、证据和复核结果的中文报告。

**不会修改代码、自动修复、提交、回滚或发布业务项目。模型报告仍需人工判断。**

## 安装

环境要求：Node.js 22 或更新版本，以及目标仓库使用的 Git 或 SVN 命令行工具。插件依赖 DSH 的工具和模型服务，不能脱离 DSH 单独运行。

在 DSH 中通过插件管理器安装并启用，或使用：

	dsh plugin add https://github.com/f-e-n-g-0531/dsh-code-review.git

升级后确认当前 DSH 进程已经加载新版本。仓库发布新版本不会自动更新正在运行的 DSH；本项目也不会自动修改已有 profile 或重启宿主。

> 许可限制：本项目采用非商业源码公开许可证。公司内部商业项目、收费服务及商业交付需要另行取得书面授权。详见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。

## 第一次使用

在目标仓库的 DSH Agent 会话中，可以这样提出请求：

> 审查 src/api.ts 和 src/client.ts 的改动。先展示审查范围和模型目的地，确认后再执行。不要修改代码。

插件提供两个工具：

1. **code_review_preview**：读取本地变更，列出审查文件、额外上下文、排除原因和模型目的地。此步骤不调用模型。
2. **code_review_execute**：接收预览返回的 previewId 和 confirmed: true。执行前重新检查文件；只有预览仍有效且宿主允许执行时，才把批准内容发送给当前 Agent 模型。

调用示例：

	{"selectedPaths":["src/api.ts","src/client.ts"],"autoContext":true}

执行参数为：

	{"previewId":"预览返回的ID","confirmed":true}

执行返回中文 Markdown 报告，以及 JSON 格式的结构化报告。代码、会话目录或模型路由变化后，需要重新预览。

## 可以审查什么

| 场景 | 支持情况 |
|---|---|
| Git 工作区 | HEAD 与工作区的净变化，包含暂存和未暂存改动；没有单独的 staged/unstaged 模式 |
| Git 单个提交 | 使用 commit 参数；与唯一父提交比较，根提交与空旧版本比较。合并提交请使用区间模式 |
| Git 两个版本 | 使用 baseRevision 和 targetRevision；比较两个版本的文件树，不自动计算合并基点 |
| SVN 工作副本 | 本地 BASE 与工作副本比较，不连接远端；不支持 SVN 历史区间审查 |
| 多个子仓库 | 用 repositoryPath 指定会话工作区中的一个仓库根目录；每个仓库分别预览和执行 |

未跟踪文件必须通过 selectedPaths 显式选入。省略 selectedPaths 时，审查范围是仓库根目录的变更，不只是当前子目录。

## 常用参数

所有文件路径都相对于本次选定的仓库，使用正斜杠；不要使用绝对路径、上级路径或链接目录。

| 参数 | 用途 | 示例 |
|---|---|---|
| selectedPaths | 只审查选中的变更文件 | ["src/api.ts"] |
| repositoryPath | 指定工作区内的子仓库 | "project-a" |
| contextPaths | 手动加入理解代码所需的文件 | ["src/types.ts"] |
| autoContext | 从变更及手动上下文寻找依赖；Git 和 SVN 最多沿三层依赖链读取 | true |
| callerScopePaths | 在指定目录中寻找引用变更文件的代码；已捕获调用方会标出调用行与唯一声明行 | ["src/clients"] |
| oldContextPaths | Git 历史审查中，只加入旧版本的上下文 | ["src/removed-helper.ts"] |
| rulePaths | 加入项目审查规则，最多四个 UTF-8 Markdown 或文本文件 | ["review-rules.md"] |
| businessRequirement | 提供业务要求；不是缺陷证据，也不会增加读取权限 | "请求失败时必须释放连接" |
| reviewRounds | 独立审查次数，1～3，默认 1；会增加模型调用量 | 2 |

commit 与 baseRevision/targetRevision 不能同时使用。oldContextPaths 只能用于 Git 历史审查。

自动上下文和引用方发现是保守的文本导航，不是编译器分析。动态导入、宏、重载、继承和实例方法可能无法解析；找到引用不等于证明函数实际被调用。历史调用方的命名导入线索逐侧对应相同版本声明，标明 side/revision；缺少该版本的批准正文不回退另一侧。Git 历史可沿修改前后两侧分别捕获最多三层依赖；SVN 可沿安全的当前工作副本节点取得最多三层依赖，不读取 SVN 历史。已批准正文中的唯一命名声明和唯一 default 导出会标出位置；同名、重导出或跨侧内容不猜测。命名空间导入后的独立成员调用可导航至唯一命名声明；写入、逃逸或间接调用不推定绑定，不是实例类型分析。

## 如何读报告

先看**覆盖情况和限制**，再看问题列表：

- completed：相应阶段完成，不表示代码绝对正确。
- partial：只完成部分工作；检查未完成文件、证据不足或预算限制。
- failed：审查执行失败，不是“审核通过”。
- cancelled：审查被取消。

每个候选问题会保留位置、触发条件、影响和复核结果。复核可能支持、反驳、无法确定或未完成；被反驳的候选不会悄悄删除。程序会核对引用的位置和原文，但这不能代替人工判断缺陷是否成立。

额外上下文被读取，不等于它已作为主文件完成审查。没有发现问题，也不证明代码没有缺陷。

## 数据与安全

- 预览会在本地读取选定变更和上下文；确认执行后，这些内容可能发送给当前模型提供方。发送前请检查范围。
- 插件沿用 DSH 正常工具权限，不额外发起一套审批；confirmed 只确认预览，不能绕过宿主权限。
- 不执行项目代码、构建脚本或模型生成的 shell 命令。模型只能在批准的快照中查找、搜索和读取。
- 常见凭据路径会被排除，但普通源码也可能含秘密。路径过滤不能代替人工检查。
- 二进制、不能解码的文件、链接和超限内容会被阻断，不会自动截断后假装完成。
- SVN 的复制、替换、切换目录、外部工作副本、冲突及部分属性状态不受支持。含 svn:keywords 的文件也会被阻断，以免把关键字展开当作代码变化。

## 默认规模限制

| 项目 | 默认上限 |
|---|---|
| 变更文件 | 200 个 |
| 单文件 | 256 KiB |
| 全部快照 | 4 MiB |
| 额外上下文 | 共 20 个文件，手动与自动来源共享 |
| 单次模型输入 | 约 96 KiB |
| 一次审查的模型调用 | 100 次，多个审查阶段共享 |

大变更可以按保留原始行号的差异窗口分批分析；不能容纳的部分会明确标为未完成。详细读取、时间和发现预算见 [开发与发布指南](DEVELOPMENT.md)。

## 文档导航

- [版本变化](CHANGELOG.md)：各版对使用者有何影响。
- [本次发布说明](RELEASE-NOTES.md)：新版本内容、升级注意事项及限制。
- [开发与发布指南](DEVELOPMENT.md)：测试、打包、发布和失败恢复。
- [核心能力对照](CORE-ALIGNMENT-TASKS.md)：已具备能力与尚未完成的差距。
- [参考源码对照](CORE-SOURCE-INVENTORY.md)：维护者使用的固定参考来源。
- [评测说明](https://github.com/f-e-n-g-0531/dsh-code-review/blob/main/evaluation/README.md)：样本、试跑观察及其证据限制。

最新安装包与正式版本以 [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@feng0531/dsh-code-review) 和 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/f-e-n-g-0531/dsh-code-review/releases) 为准。发布与安装成功不代表真实模型的误报率或漏报率已经得到证明。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# DSH VCS

在 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）Web 中查看 Git / SVN 文件变更和提交历史的**只读插件**。

你可以查看差异、浏览历史、追溯文件，但不能通过本插件修改文件、暂存、提交、拉取或推送。

- npm 包：`@feng0531/dsh-vcs`
- [下载正式版本](https://github.com/f-e-n-g-0531/dsh-vcs/releases/latest) · [查看更新](https://github.com/f-e-n-g-0531/dsh-vcs/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
- 采用[非商业许可证](<LICENSE>)，商业用途须另行书面授权。

## 能做什么

| 场景 | 功能 |
| --- | --- |
| 查看工作区变更 | Git 全部、已暂存、未暂存文件；SVN 本地基线与工作副本、属性差异 |
| 阅读代码差异 | 默认 Monaco 只读 Diff，支持并排／行内、换行、忽略行尾空白、上一处／下一处差异 |
| 浏览 Git 历史 | 搜索提交说明、作者、路径与提交时间范围（since/until，含边界，按 committer date）；查看本地分支、提交图、提交详情与目录 |
| 比较历史版本 | 比较提交与选定父提交，或选择两个本地提交进行 A/B 比较 |
| 追溯代码来源 | 文件历史、唯一来源重命名追踪（含改名同时修改）、Blame（逐行查看最后修改者和提交） |
| 查看其他内容 | 支持部分静态图片比较；较大历史 UTF-8 文件可分段阅读 |
| 浏览 SVN 历史 | 明确同意连接后，查看 HTTPS 仓库日志、修订差异和文件历史 |

提供中英文界面。编辑器加载失败时会显示基础文本比较；它不是完整的 Monaco 替代品。

## 安装

需要：

- Node.js **22 或更新版本**。
- DSH Web：声明兼容 **0.1.7-rc.2 或 0.2.0-rc.2**。
- 系统 PATH 中有 Git 或 SVN；只使用 Git 时无需安装 SVN。

profile是DSH的配置和插件环境，不是Session。下面的web是示例，请先确认运行中的DSH使用哪个profile；若不同，替换命令中的web。宿主插件命令通过pnpm执行，需确保该工具可用。

在终端执行：

	dsh plugin --profile web add @feng0531/dsh-vcs@0.3.73

安装后由你自行重启 DSH，再刷新原来的 Web 页面。安装会改变所选 profile；升级前请备份配置。**本项目的发布不会自动升级或重启你的 DSH。**

也可以从 [GitHub Release](https://github.com/f-e-n-g-0531/dsh-vcs/releases/latest) 下载 tgz 和校验文件，核对 SHA-256 后安装：

	dsh plugin --profile web add "<tgz 的绝对路径>"

升级、旧包迁移和回滚见[安装指南](https://github.com/f-e-n-g-0531/dsh-vcs/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md)。

## 开始使用

1. 在 DSH 中选择一个 Session，确认它的工作目录在项目内。
2. 打开 VCS 页面，发现仓库，再从顶部下拉框选择仓库。
3. 点击文件查看差异，或进入历史视图浏览提交。
4. SVN远程历史需先审阅并明确同意。复制成员可主动查看范围内的固定来源历史，不自动跨复制追溯。
5. 外部工具修改了项目后，手动刷新；可见窗口重新获得焦点时也会刷新。没有定时轮询。

默认发现当前目录、一级子目录以及包含当前目录的上级仓库。项目更深时，输入相对 Session 目录的子目录，例如 `packages/example`；不接受任意绝对路径或越界路径。

**注意：Session 位于仓库子目录时，发现后的查看范围可以覆盖整个仓库。**

### 左右两侧比较的是什么

| 模式 | 左侧 | 右侧 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Git 全部 | 最近提交（HEAD） | 当前工作区 |
| Git 已暂存 | 最近提交（HEAD） | 暂存区（Index） |
| Git 未暂存 | 暂存区（Index） | 当前工作区 |
| SVN 本地变更 | 本地基线（BASE） | 当前工作副本 |

新增文件可能使用空白左侧。冲突文件只供查看，不提供三方合并或冲突解决。

### SVN 历史需要单独同意

本地 SVN 变更比较不连接服务器。打开远程历史前，需要审阅服务器与路径范围并勾选同意；授权约 5 分钟后过期，须重新手动同意。

目前仅支持系统信任、**无需额外认证的 HTTPS SVN 服务**。不提供用户名／密码、自定义证书或其他协议。历史范围固定在本地工作副本的修订，不自动获取服务器最新版本。

## 目前的限制

- **不是完整的 Fork 客户端**：没有仓库写操作，历史图和列表都有容量限制；分支导航使用本地分支、标签及本地缓存的远程跟踪引用，不连接远端、不 fetch。
- 普通文本比较每侧最多 **2MiB**。Git提交／A-B／工作区三个模式比较超限时可手动加载完整UTF-8文本，每侧最多 **8MiB、10万行**，单行最多65536字符；计算超时会明确提示结果不完整。工作区读取期间发生变化会拒绝结果，但不是系统级原子快照；SVN大文件仍不支持。
- 历史 UTF-8 正文分段最多 **16MiB**；分段阅读不是完整Diff，与上述完整比较是不同功能。
- 重命名追溯仅沿第一父链，至少50%相似且确认唯一删除源／新增目标；合并、复制、歧义或累计32次确认后停止。
- 子模块变更只显示 Index 记录的提交指针与本地检出状态（已检出／未初始化／目录缺失／不可读）；不进入子模块、不读取其 HEAD，也不更新或同步。
- 树浏览和来源行预览可手动查看该历史路径的文件历史，并可选跟随重命名；路径必须存在于所选提交，跟随规则与路径历史一致（第一父链、≥50%相似、唯一确认、32次上限）。
- 冲突文件可额外手动查看 Git Index 阶段1／2／3，任意两阶段可只读比较。缺失阶段显示为空、不推断原内容；阶段编号不声称合并／变基归属。每阶段仍为 2MiB 预览；不读取工作文件、不解决冲突，子模块只显示提交引用，链接只显示目标文本。
- 图片支持 PNG、基线 JPEG 和简单静态 VP8／无损VP8L WebP；动画、扩展 WebP 等不支持。
- 支持 UTF-8、GBK、带 BOM 的 UTF-16；不是通用编码检测器。
- 取消状态／比较请求不保证立即停止底层进程，进程仍受超时和输出上限控制。

## 常见问题

- **找不到仓库**：检查 Session 工作目录和 Git／SVN 的 PATH；更深项目使用相对子目录发现。
- **提示重新发现**：目录变了或发现授权过期，手动重新发现即可。
- **高级编辑器加载失败**：确认安装了完整正式包并重新加载宿主；失败时仍可使用基础比较。
- **SVN 历史连接失败**：先确认是受信任 HTTPS 服务，且不要求本插件未支持的额外认证。

正式版本通过自动测试、Windows／Linux 检查和隔离浏览器回归。**这些不证明你的当前 DSH 页面已加载新版，也不代替你的实际环境验证。**

## 开发与更多资料

[文档导航](https://github.com/f-e-n-g-0531/dsh-vcs/blob/main/docs/README.md) · [贡献指南](https://github.com/f-e-n-g-0531/dsh-vcs/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) · [安全说明](https://github.com/f-e-n-g-0531/dsh-vcs/blob/main/SECURITY.md) · [维护者发布流程](<docs/RELEASING.md>)

dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck

**中文** · [English](docs/README.en.md) **拨开战争迷雾看见终点，剩下的交给 MattSkillsDeck。** 让 [mattpocock/skills](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills) 在 DSH 里化作一块看得见、派得动的任务板。 你的 ⭐是我夜空中最亮的星。 *Part the fog of war, see the end — MattSkillsDeck handles the rest.* [![版本](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck?label=%E7%89%88%E6%9C%AC)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck) [![下载量](https://img.shields.io/badge/dynamic/json?url=https%3A%2F%2Fapi.npmjs.org%2Fdownloads%2Fpoint%2Flast-month%2Fdsh-mattpocock-skills-deck&query=%24.downloads&label=%E4%B8%8B%E8%BD%BD%E9%87%8F&suffix=%2F%E6%9C%88&color=brightgreen)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck) [![下载总量](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck?label=%E4%B8%8B%E8%BD%BD%E6%80%BB%E9%87%8F&color=red)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck) [![最近更新](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/FeatherHunter/dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck?label=%E6%9C%80%E8%BF%91%E6%9B%B4%E6%96%B0&color=FE7D37)](https://github.com/FeatherHunter/dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck/commits/main) [![月提交](https://img.shields.io/github/commit-activity/m/FeatherHunter/dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck?label=%E6%8F%90%E4%BA%A4%E6%95%B0&color=DFAB01)](https://github.com/FeatherHunter/dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck/graphs/commit-activity) [![许可证](https://img.shields.io/badge/%E8%AE%B8%E5%8F%AF%E8%AF%81-MIT-lightgrey.svg)](LICENSE) [![技能包](https://img.shields.io/badge/%E6%8A%80%E8%83%BD%E5%8C%85-mattpocock%2Fskills-9D7CD8)](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills) [![期待你参与](https://img.shields.io/badge/%E6%9C%9F%E5%BE%85%E4%BD%A0%E5%8F%82%E4%B8%8E-brightgreen.svg)](https://github.com/FeatherHunter/dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck/issues)

INSTALL
安装

前置要求：[DSH](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh)（DeepSeek Harness）。在 DSH 里，你下指令、AI 干活；MattSkillsDeck 把这些活变成面板上的任务。 任务板绑定的仓库需要写权限：新建标签要 push 权限，给票打标签要 triage 及以上权限；只有读权限时能建票、能读票，但补标签、标签流转与 wayfinder 标签都不可用。
```bash # ① 安装 DSH CLI（已装跳过） npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh # ② 安装 MattSkillsDeck —— --profile 必填：装进你实际使用的 DSH 入口对应的 profile # （装错 profile 等于没装，重启多少次都不会加载） dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck # 用自启 web 服务（dsh web） # 或者 dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck # 用 DSH Desktop 桌面应用 # 锁定最新版更稳（当前 1.7.51）： dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck@1.7.51 --registry https://registry.npmjs.org # 或者 dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck@1.7.51 --registry https://registry.npmjs.org ```
装完**重启一次对应的 DSH 入口**即生效：桌面应用完全退出并重开 DSH Desktop；web 服务重启 `dsh web` 后刷新页面。零配置。 **右侧面板性能极致优化：点击到内容可见，真机实测从 5075 毫秒降到 193 毫秒，性能提升约 96.2%（约 26 倍）。** 面板就开在 DSH 自己的右侧边栏里：左边列表、右边详情，并排看。不需要再装别的插件。 **👇 装完重启，面板就绪就是这个样子。**
进阶安装：免全局、更新不生效、交给 AI 下面命令以 web profile 为例——**DSH Desktop 桌面应用用户请把所有 `--profile web` 换成 `--profile desktop`**。 ```bash # 免全局安装（想更稳，像上面一样锁版本） npx --yes @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck # 更新被静默忽略时，显式指定官方源 dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck@latest --registry https://registry.npmjs.org ``` 复制下面这段发给你的 AI，它会确认 profile、检查环境并按需安装： ```text 请帮我安装 DeepSeek Harness 插件 dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck（MattSkillsDeck）。 先读仓库 README：https://github.com/FeatherHunter/dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck 先确认我实际使用的 DSH 入口对应哪个 profile（DSH Desktop 桌面应用 → desktop；自启 web 服务 → web），把插件装进正确的 profile； 然后自行检查环境并按需安装（已装的跳过），完成后简要汇报结果。 ```
升级 · 卸载（desktop profile 用户把 `--profile web` 换成 `--profile desktop`）： ```bash dsh plugin --profile web update dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck # 升级 dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck # 卸载 ```

BOARD
任务板列表

仓库里的任务不再是流水账：面板把它们按可接、阻塞、已关闭归位，进度走到哪一格一眼看清。每行任务的按钮就是动作入口：点一下，写好的指令填进输入框，确认后再发送。地图类型的行永远置顶，已关闭的收成一行。 **👇 任务在哪看、状态怎么筛，全在这张图。**

STATUSBAR
底部任务栏

每条会话输入框下面都有一条胶囊状态栏：可接数量、待修（BUG）数量、诊断、沉淀、交接、环境进度都在上面。点可接、环境等主要分段，即跳到对应面板页，看完即回，不打断手头会话。 **👇 离手最近的操作条，完整一条长这样。**

DETAIL
ISSUE 详情与评论

点开任意一条任务，描述、标签、认领人与评论都在面板里排好版，不用跳终端。在底部输入框直接回话，一般只按标签显示其中一个（诊断、修复、讨论、执行），需要另起再点新会话。 **👇 点开一条任务，看透并回上话。**

NEW SESSION
新会话

任何活都能另起干净会话干：详情页顶部点新会话，新会话标题自动起好，承接指令已预填，人只管检查后发送。当前会话不受扰，脏活累活都在新会话里。 **👇 点一下新会话，指令已预填等人发。**

SKILLS
技能快捷入口

随包 27 个技能（快照 v1.3.1）装好即用：面板技能页顶部给通用推荐（默认 /ask-matt），列表一行讲清一个技能的中文用途，点加载就把斜杠指令填进输入框。完整名单与教程见 Matt 官方 [aihero.dev/skills](https://www.aihero.dev/skills)，本插件只讲入口与推荐。

BACKENDS
多后端切换

同一个面板可换跑道：设置页后端选择器列出 GitHub、本地 Markdown、GitLab 与 Other（无后端）逃生舱。切换只换数据源：切换后原数据不可见，原后端数据保留，切回来又可见。新人第一次大多只用一条跑道，知道能换即可。 **👇 换跑道不断数据，选择器长这样。**

FAQ
常见问题

更新之后还是旧版本？ 这是 DSH 桌面端的 pnpm 供应链策略（`minimumReleaseAge`）导致的：刚发布的版本，几个小时内 `dsh plugin update` 和插件市场的「更新」按钮都会静默跳过。更新后请完全退出 DSH 再重开，按 Ctrl+F5 刷新页面；还没更新的话，显式指定官方源装一次： ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck@latest --registry https://registry.npmjs.org ``` **👇 官方源装最新版，成功回显长这样。**
更新报错找不到新版本（No matching version），地址是镜像源？ 这是镜像源还没有同步到新版本：报错地址写着镜像源（例如 `registry.npmmirror.com`），而新版本已经在官方源上发布，包本身没有漏发。等镜像源同步完成就能正常更新；着急用的话，显式指定官方源装一次（下面这条命令不要去掉末尾的源参数，去掉就会走回镜像源）： ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-mattpocock-skills-deck@latest --registry https://registry.npmjs.org ``` 桌面应用用户把 `--profile web` 换成 `--profile desktop`。

JOIN
欢迎您加入我们

非常欢迎提交PR、共同维护项目，现在迭代中很缺对markdown后端的开发和完善，Gitlab目前无人力开发。
